what_happened: Defect B's Condition 7 correction was derived from Mathlib master's live longFile linter source (fetched via web-fetch delegate) and verified exactly against both cited data points (2967 lines->3100, 3200 lines->3400), rather than trusting the task's own hypothesis unchecked.

Defect A's naive remedy (adding planner-agent to the lean index-entries.json entry's agents[]) was mechanically disproven by reading context-discovery.md's documented OR-based adaptive query: since planner-agent is a cross-domain shared agent, that fix would leak lean-specific guidance into every other domain's plan dispatches. Caught before recommending it.

The pinned Mathlib source for the originating repo's toolchain (lean-toolchain v4.33.0-rc1; lake-manifest mathlib rev 79d0395a1825a6264ad5d269e35e60537518955e) is reachable locally at /home/benjamin/Projects/BimodalLogic/.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Tactic/Linter/Style.lean. Read it directly at plan time: candidate = max((lastLine/100)*100+200, defValue=1500), accept iff linterBound == candidate || linterBound + 100 == candidate. This closes the research report's named risk (master-vs-pinned drift) without scheduling a web re-check phase.

This task's own edits trip a coupled generated surface in THIS repository: check-extension-docs.sh Rule R (verify-deploy Gate 3) enforces index-entries.json line_count accuracy for every edited context file, and Gate 5 content-hash-compares the deployed tree against the source store, so a full-gate pass requires a deploy-headless.sh regeneration. Neither is commit-blocking here (no pre-commit hook is installed in this repo), so per the obligation being authored both are declared and scheduled in the plan's final reconciliation phase rather than per-phase.

suite_selection_select returns a DIFFERENT suite set depending on which copy of the identical library is sourced: the source-store copy returns 4 suites for plan-format.md, the deployed copy returns 5 (adding the lean-provided test-lean-challenge-snapshot.sh). The libraries are byte-identical; the divergence is the corpus they scan -- the deployed tests/ directory aggregates every extension's suites while core's source tests/ holds only core's. A Tier Justification measured against the source-store copy warns under the deployed validate-artifact.sh check. Resolved by measuring against the deployed copy and naming the deployed run-all.sh entry point.

Phase 2's own Verification bullet claims 'a declared 3300 against 3200 lines is rejected by N == candidate || N + 100 == candidate'. Hand-applying the corrected formula shows the opposite: candidate=3400 for 3200 lines, accepted set = {candidate-100, candidate} = {3300, 3400}, so a declared baseline of 3300 IS accepted (no warning), not rejected. The two measurement reproductions (2967->3100, 3200->3400) the same bullet names are both correct and were verified by hand. The Condition 7 prose written to the file states only the verified, correct rule (not the erroneous 3300 example), so no file content is wrong -- only this one plan verification illustration is inaccurate. Not fixed in the plan itself since Tasks checklist items, not Verification bullets, are this agent's edit authority for plan content beyond checkoff annotation.
